records.name: Project Moshen Dance Company
records.summary: An all-female jazz dance company in Philadelphia that performs two shows a year, visits schools, and teaches master classes at local universities.
records.what_you_do: Come to one of the company's shows, book a school visit or master class, or audition to dance with the company.

schedule.text: Two shows a year, plus master classes at local universities and school visits. No regular class schedule is published.

first_step.how: Sign up for the company email list for show dates, or use the audition link on the Contact Us page to ask about dancing with the company
first_step.basis: Shows and master classes are open to the public and the site has a sign-up list; joining the dancers needs an audition.

records.notes: Newest dated item found is a 2019 magazine article linked from the site (dated from its URL, April 28, 2019). The homepage shows no dates, so the dormant status rests on that one item. Worth a check by email before we promote it.

records.name: Quintessence Theatre Group
records.summary: A theatre company in residence at the Sedgwick Theater in Mt. Airy. It stages a season of plays and runs classes, student matinees and a summer camp.
records.what_you_do: Buy tickets to a season show, take an adult class or workshop, or bring a student group. The site has a Volunteer page for helping with the company; its roles are not described in the page text.

schedule.text: Plays run in a yearly season (Season XVII is current), with adult classes and workshops on the education page. Exact class dates are not in the page text.

cost.text: Ticket prices listed on the site

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to a Season XVII show, or sign up for the QMail newsletter to hear about classes and volunteer openings
first_step.basis: Shows are public and sold by ticket, and the site lists adult classes and a volunteer page with no application step shown.

records.notes: The old address QTGrep.org redirects to quintessencetheatre.org. The homepage has a current season and a fall run image labelled with dates but no year, so the status is probably active rather than dated. Public way in is attending shows and taking classes; the volunteer page is linked but was not read.

records.name: Range of Motion Philly
records.summary: A studio in Center City with martial arts, parkour, dance and music classes for kids, teens and adults, plus school break camps and a summer camp.
records.what_you_do: Join an after-school or summer class, try an adult martial arts or street dance class, or email for a free trial martial arts lesson.

schedule.text: After-school classes during the school year, school closing camps, a summer camp, and adult classes. The full class schedule is on the site.

cost.text: An intro month is listed at $25. Early registration discounts are offered on the site.

first_step.how: Email Rangeofmotion@gmail.com for a free trial martial arts lesson, or register for an intro month through the Register Today link
first_step.basis: The site names an intro month and a free trial lesson for newcomers and says how to start.

records.notes: The homepage gives early registration deadlines for the 2026/27 school year (September 30 and October 30), and the year is taken from that school year label. The batch lists this group as a nonprofit, but the site presents it as a studio with paid classes. The site does not say whether it is a nonprofit, so the kind is set to program. Urban Movement Arts is named as a partner on the site and is listed in leads_only.

records.name: Rebel Arts Movement
records.summary: A Philadelphia circus arts and gymnastics studio.
records.what_you_do: Take a circus or gymnastics class or check the site for open studio hours and current registration.

cost.text: Not confirmed from the group's own pages

first_step.how: Visit the website for current classes and how to register

records.notes: The group's homepage returned only its title ('Rebel Arts Movement | Circus Arts & Gymnastics') on both attempts, so no class, schedule, contact or dated item could be read from it. A web search (not the group's own page) said the studio was founded in 2020, offers acrobatics, tumbling and aerial classes mostly for kids and teens, and that a performance company called The Rebellion Circus sits under it. Those details are unverified and are not in the record. The search also turned up an older, different gym named Rebel Circus Arts in Port Richmond, which is not this group. Needs a human check of the live site before it is promoted.

records.name: Soil Generation
records.summary: A collective of Black and Brown women and gender-expansive people who work on access to land, growing food, and healing, with campaigns on urban farming and climate justice.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for the newsletter or write to the group by email to find out about its campaigns and cultural projects. No volunteer roles or class schedule are published.

schedule.text: No schedule is published. Campaigns and projects are announced on the site and social media.

first_step.how: Email soilgen215@gmail.com or join the newsletter to ask how to get involved in a campaign
first_step.basis: Public email and newsletter sign-up with no application listed, though the site does not describe a newcomer step.

records.notes: The site is working and lists current campaigns and a recent journal article, but the article has no date, so there is no dated sign of life. The newsletter form on the site says it 'needs a storage option', so the sign-up may not be working. Audience is written as women because the group's own description centres Black and Brown women and gender-expansive people; the site does not say whether the community field is a membership rule.

records.name: Spells Writing Lab, Inc.
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps school-age children build creative and expository writing skills through free writing programs, classroom visits, and workshops for teachers.
records.what_you_do: Apply online to volunteer as a classroom writing mentor, a Write Club tutor, or a workshop helper, then attend an orientation. You can also register for a workshop or ask for a classroom visit.

schedule.text: Volunteer orientations are held on weeknights in Center City, with one planned on Drexel University's campus; dates are announced on the site. Workshops are listed on the registration page.

cost.text: Volunteering and workshop programs are listed as free

first_step.how: Submit the online volunteer application on phillyspells.org, then attend the next orientation
first_step.basis: Orientations are open and the online form is simple, though volunteers must apply and attend an orientation first.

records.notes: The site lists summer writing camp internships and upcoming volunteer opportunities, but none of its items show a date. No address, email or phone is published on the homepage; the contact and directions pages exist but were not read, so contacts are limited to the website and social links.

records.name: Spiral Q
records.summary: A Philadelphia arts organization that uses art to connect students, neighbors and activists around justice and joy, with school-based programs and community events.
records.what_you_do: Join the mailing list, donate supplies or money, or check the jobs page. The site does not describe a volunteer or class schedule.

schedule.text: No schedule is published. The site names current projects, including SPARQ in schools and Peoplehood 2026, without dates.

first_step.how: Email community@spiralq.org or join the mailing list to ask about the next project
first_step.basis: A public mailing list and contact address are offered, with no application listed.

records.notes: The site names a 2026 project (Peoplehood 2026) but gives no dates on any event or news item, so the status is probably active rather than dated. Public way in is the mailing list and getting in touch; the group's programs are mostly in schools. No street address is published.

records.name: Stenton, NSCDA/PA
records.summary: The Stenton historic house museum in North Philadelphia, run by the Colonial Dames of America in Pennsylvania. It offers free second Saturday tours, history programs and seasonal events.
records.what_you_do: Come to a free second Saturday house tour, a history program or the Halloween Harvest Festival, or support the Friends of Stenton. Volunteer roles are not listed on the site.

schedule.text: Free second Saturday house tours at 12, 1, 2 and 3 pm. October 10 has a symposium (10 am to 2 pm, $20) and a free chocolate demonstration (2 to 3 pm). The Halloween Harvest Festival runs October 24, 1 to 3 pm.

cost.text: Second Saturday tours are free. The October 10 symposium is $20.

first_step.how: Come to the free second Saturday tour, or RSVP for an event through the programs page at stenton.org/programs
first_step.basis: Tours and several events are free and open to the public, and the site says how to RSVP for others.

records.notes: The event dates on the site have no year. The year 2026 is inferred because October 10 and October 24 fall on Saturdays in 2026, matching the 'second Saturday' tours. The museum's Friends of Stenton support group is part of the same listing. Batch kind is nonprofit; the museum is run by a society, so kind is kept as nonprofit.

records.name: Swim Pony Performing Arts
records.summary: A Philadelphia theatre company that makes immersive and playful devised shows, including interactive work that takes place in unusual spaces.
records.what_you_do: Come to one of the company's immersive shows, or use the Can I Help? page on the site to ask how to support or volunteer. The page text did not show what that page offers.

schedule.text: Show dates are not shown on the site. Its featured show, The Stupidest, Scariest Time, has no date on the page.

first_step.how: Use the contact page to ask about the next show, or the Can I Help? page to offer help
first_step.basis: Shows are public events; the site offers a contact page and an open help page with no application step shown.

records.notes: The site works but has no dated item at all. Its newest dated listings in older material are from the 2014 to 2016 seasons. A web search found no 2025 or 2026 Swim Pony show, only a 2010 listing. Status is probably active only because the site is up; a human should confirm recent activity before promoting. No address, email or phone is published on the site.

records.name: Tangle Movement Arts
records.summary: An aerial dance theatre company in Philadelphia that makes circus shows and teaches private and small group aerial and trapeze lessons, with a sliding scale on lesson prices.
records.what_you_do: Book aerial or trapeze lessons with the instructor for one to four people, or join the email list for studio jams and community events for aerial and circus artists.

schedule.text: Lessons are booked with the instructor on a time that fits both people, with Wednesday daytime, weekend mornings and some evenings. Lessons can be weekly, every other week, monthly, or single.

cost.text: $60 to $95 per lesson for one or two people on a sliding scale ($75 is the stated true cost); $90 to $120 for three or four people. Paid by Venmo, PayPal or Cash App at the end of each lesson.

first_step.how: Email lauren@tangle-arts.com or call or text 215-266-6215 to talk about your goals and book a first lesson
first_step.basis: The class page says single lessons are welcome and that beginners get a plan tailored to them, and it gives the way to start.

records.notes: Status is dormant because the newest dated item is the 2022 show Force the Mirror Open. The classes page reads as current (lessons offered, rates listed), but it has no dates, and the studio jams are described as new with no dates. Human check recommended. The batch lists this as a nonprofit and the site does not say so; kind is kept from the batch seed.

records.name: Temple Contemporary
records.summary: A free contemporary art gallery on the first floor of Temple's Tyler School of Art and Architecture. It has exhibitions, lectures and public events for anyone to attend.
records.what_you_do: Visit the free exhibitions during open hours, or come to a public event such as the October 15 game night or the October 30 evening program. The page lists no public volunteer, docent, class or workshop program.

schedule.text: Open Tuesday to Saturday, 11 am to 6 pm, with free admission. Upcoming events include an October 15 game night (5 to 6:30 pm) and an October 30 evening program (5 to 6:30 pm). Exhibitions run to December 5, 2026.

locations.label: Temple Contemporary gallery, Norris Street entrance

first_step.how: Stop by during open hours, or check the Tyler events listings and come to a public event
first_step.basis: Free and open to the public with posted hours and events that anyone can attend.

records.notes: A gallery is a venue, not a membership group, so the way in is attending. Category and interest are the closest tags; no tag fits exhibitions exactly. The 215-777-9000 number is Tyler's main line from the footer, not a gallery line. No gallery email is published; staff addresses are on the page but were not recorded.

records.name: Temple University Music Preparatory Division
records.summary: The non-credit music and dance division of Temple's Boyer College of Music and Dance. It offers lessons and classes for people of all ages, from infants to adults.
records.what_you_do: Enroll in individual lessons (including Suzuki instruction) through Temple's non-credit course search. Music Prep also has an email list for news.

schedule.text: Lessons and classes run year round for all ages. Enrollment is through the non-credit course search. Specific class times are not on the page.

cost.text: Tuition and fees are not published on the page

first_step.how: Submit the Individual Lessons Application through the Temple non-credit course search, or join the Music Prep email list
first_step.basis: Lessons are open to all ages through a standard application, and the page lists no audition requirement.

records.notes: The page names no instruments, ensembles or dance classes, so the dance side is not recorded. The page has no dated event or deadline, so status is probably active from the working site. The contact page returned 404 and no email or phone was published on this page.

leads_only.name: Urban Movement Arts
leads_only.note: Named as a partner on the Range of Motion site for its adult street dance program (UMA Dip Program). Not checked.

leads_only.name: The Rebellion Circus
leads_only.note: Named in a web search as a performance company under Rebel Arts Movement, founded 2024. Not checked on its own site.

leads_only.name: Friends of Stenton
leads_only.note: Support group named on the Stenton site with its own newsletter and donation page. Folded into the Stenton record, not checked separately.

notes: Rebel Arts Movement's homepage returned only its title on both attempts, so its record is thin (status unknown, confidence low). Several groups (Swim Pony, Tangle Movement Arts, Spiral Q, Soil Generation, Temple Music Prep, Spells Writing Lab) have live sites with no dated items, so their status is probably active or dormant by rule and needs a human check. Tangle Movement Arts is dormant by dated evidence (2022) even though its classes page reads as current. Two WebSearch calls were used: one for Rebel Arts Movement and one for Swim Pony, and the search results were used only as leads and context, not as recorded facts for Swim Pony. Redirects followed: QTGrep.org to quintessencetheatre.org, and rangeofmotionphilly.com to romcommunity.com. Fetch use was 17 of 60 and no blocked pages were seen. All 12 groups were checked.
